vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-tasks
Version: 1.0.8

The skill bundle is a standard interface for managing Google Tasks via a 'gws' CLI tool. The SKILL.md file provides legitimate API documentation for task and task list operations (CRUD) and lacks any indicators of malicious intent, such as data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or prompt injection attacks.

llm.summary: The skill's purpose (manage Google Tasks via the 'gws' CLI) is plausible, but the runtime instructions ask the agent to read or create a shared SKILL.md outside the skill directory and do not declare how authentication/credentials are handled, which is inconsistent and worth caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description align with requiring the 'gws' binary — that is coherent. However the SKILL.md delegates authentication and global flags to a separate ../gws-shared/SKILL.md which is not included or declared in the skill metadata (no required env vars or primary credential). The delegation is reasonable in principle but the omission of any declared auth mechanism is an unexplained gap.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly tell the agent to read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules and, if missing, to run 'gws generate-skills' to create it. That requires the agent to access a file outside the skill's directory and potentially write new files on disk. The SKILL.md also tells the agent to run arbitrary 'gws tasks ...' and 'gws schema ...' commands which will operate under whatever credentials the 'gws' CLI has — but the document does not limit or describe what data may be read or transmitted, nor what credential store 'gws' will use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is an instruction-only skill. That reduces supply-chain risk because nothing in the skill package will be written or executed by default by the installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential, yet Google Tasks access requires authorization. The SKILL.md defers auth to an external shared file and the 'gws' CLI, meaning credentials may be read from local config, OAuth caches, or other places without being declared. The lack of explicit credential declarations makes it unclear what secrets the agent will rely on or access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal), but instructions include running 'gws generate-skills' to create ../gws-shared/SKILL.md if missing. That action writes files outside the skill folder and could modify shared configuration used by other skills. Combined with autonomous invocation (the platform default), this increases the potential blast radius if the 'gws' CLI or the generated file contains unexpected behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a thin adapter around a local 'gws' CLI to manage Google Tasks. Before installing: 1) Confirm you trust the 'gws' binary (where it comes from and what it does) because the skill relies entirely on it. 2) Inspect the referenced ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or the file 'gws generate-skills' would create) to see exactly how authentication is performed and what credentials/config files will be read or written. 3) Be cautious about allowing the agent to run 'gws generate-skills' since it will create files outside the skill directory and could affect other skills. 4) Run the CLI in a sandbox or with limited Google account scopes if possible, and review OAuth consent/scopes that 'gws' requests. If you can, ask the skill author for the shared SKILL.md or for explicit documentation of the auth flow before enabling this skill.
llm.findings: [no-findings] expected: The static regex scanner found nothing. This skill is instruction-only (no code files), so the scanner had no code to analyze; the primary surface to review is SKILL.md.
